stem: A 68-year-old male with a longstanding history of Paget disease of bone presents with rapidly progressive pain in his right thigh. Radiographs demonstrate a destructive lesion arising within an expanded, previously remodeled femur. Biopsy reveals highly atypical spindle-shaped cells producing an irregular mineralized extracellular matrix. Which of the following diagnoses best explains this patient's new symptoms?
explanation: Paget disease predisposes to secondary osteosarcoma, a malignancy producing osteoid directly from atypical cells.
optionFeedback: Giant cell tumor is characterized by stromal cells and reactive giant cells, not malignant osteoid.
Paget disease predisposes to secondary osteosarcoma, a malignancy producing osteoid directly from atypical cells.
Chondrosarcoma produces malignant cartilage rather than osteoid.
Fibrous dysplasia is a benign fibro-osseous process.

distractors.A: Giant cell tumor is characterized by stromal cells and reactive giant cells, not malignant osteoid.
distractors.C: Chondrosarcoma produces malignant cartilage rather than osteoid.
distractors.D: Fibrous dysplasia is a benign fibro-osseous process.

stem: A 17-year-old female undergoes evaluation of a painful proximal tibial lesion. Radiographs demonstrate cortical destruction and elevation of the periosteum, producing a triangular region of new bone at the margin of the lesion. Which of the following mechanisms most directly accounts for the formation of this radiographic finding?
options: Uniform calcification within a benign cartilaginous matrix
Expansion of a cortical nidus with surrounding sclerosis
Development of a cartilage-capped metaphyseal projection
Rapid tumor growth that elevates the periosteum before continuous new bone can form
explanation: A Codman triangle forms when aggressive growth lifts periosteum faster than a continuous bony shell can form.
optionFeedback: Cartilage mineralization can form rings and arcs, not this periosteal triangle.
A cortical nidus with sclerosis suggests osteoid osteoma.
A cartilage-capped projection describes osteochondroma.
A Codman triangle forms when aggressive growth lifts periosteum faster than a continuous bony shell can form.

distractors.A: Cartilage mineralization can form rings and arcs, not this periosteal triangle.
distractors.B: A cortical nidus with sclerosis suggests osteoid osteoma.
distractors.C: A cartilage-capped projection describes osteochondroma.

stem: A 21-year-old male with a history of multiple hereditary exostoses undergoes genetic counseling. His father and younger sister have similar lesions involving several long bones. Genetic analysis identifies a pathogenic variant affecting a protein involved in heparan sulfate synthesis. Which of the following genes is most likely affected?
explanation: EXT1 and EXT2 encode proteins involved in heparan sulfate synthesis and are implicated in hereditary multiple osteochondromas.
optionFeedback: EXT1 and EXT2 encode proteins involved in heparan sulfate synthesis and are implicated in hereditary multiple osteochondromas.
IDH1 mutations occur in several cartilaginous neoplasms.
H3F3A mutations typify giant cell tumor.
TP53 is implicated in Li-Fraumeni syndrome.

distractors.B: IDH1 mutations occur in several cartilaginous neoplasms.
distractors.C: H3F3A mutations typify giant cell tumor.
distractors.D: TP53 is implicated in Li-Fraumeni syndrome.

stem: A 16-year-old male presents with progressive shoulder pain and swelling. Biopsy of a proximal humeral mass demonstrates pleomorphic malignant cells producing osteoid. Following confirmation of the diagnosis, the physician orders additional imaging to evaluate for distant metastatic disease. Which of the following organs is the most likely site of hematogenous metastasis?
explanation: Osteosarcoma frequently spreads hematogenously to the lungs.
optionFeedback: Splenic metastasis is not the typical first pattern.
Pancreatic metastasis is uncommon.
Osteosarcoma frequently spreads hematogenously to the lungs.
Thyroid metastasis is not the predominant pattern.

distractors.A: Splenic metastasis is not the typical first pattern.
distractors.B: Pancreatic metastasis is uncommon.
distractors.D: Thyroid metastasis is not the predominant pattern.

stem: A 10-year-old boy presents with persistent pelvic pain, intermittent fever, and elevated inflammatory markers. Initial clinical findings raise concern for osteomyelitis. However, biopsy reveals a densely cellular neoplasm composed of monotonous round cells without identifiable osteoid or cartilage formation. Which of the following immunohistochemical findings would most strongly support the suspected malignant diagnosis?
explanation: Diffuse membranous CD99 supports Ewing sarcoma in this clinical context, although it is not entirely specific.
optionFeedback: Desmin supports muscle differentiation, as in rhabdomyosarcoma.
Diffuse membranous CD99 supports Ewing sarcoma in this clinical context, although it is not entirely specific.
MDM2 overexpression supports certain liposarcomas and low-grade osteosarcomas.
Nuclear beta-catenin supports desmoid-type fibromatosis.

distractors.A: Desmin supports muscle differentiation, as in rhabdomyosarcoma.
distractors.C: MDM2 overexpression supports certain liposarcomas and low-grade osteosarcomas.
distractors.D: Nuclear beta-catenin supports desmoid-type fibromatosis.

stem: A 24-year-old female presents with an enlarging, painful lesion involving the proximal tibial epiphysis. Histologic examination demonstrates abundant multinucleated giant cells surrounded by mononuclear stromal cells with similar nuclear morphology. Molecular analysis identifies an H3F3A mutation. Which of the following cellular populations represents the primary neoplastic component of this lesion?
explanation: The mononuclear stromal cells of giant cell tumor harbor the characteristic mutation and recruit osteoclast-like giant cells.
optionFeedback: Osteoclasts are recruited by neoplastic stromal cells.
Reactive macrophages are not the primary neoplastic population.
Giant cells are reactive osteoclast-like cells.
The mononuclear stromal cells of giant cell tumor harbor the characteristic mutation and recruit osteoclast-like giant cells.

distractors.A: Osteoclasts are recruited by neoplastic stromal cells.
distractors.B: Reactive macrophages are not the primary neoplastic population.
distractors.C: Giant cells are reactive osteoclast-like cells.

stem: A 15-year-old male presents with several months of localized femoral pain. CT demonstrates a small cortical lesion containing a central nidus and substantial surrounding reactive sclerosis. Oral anti-inflammatory medication provides temporary relief, but the patient wishes to pursue definitive treatment because of persistent symptoms. Which of the following treatment modalities most directly destroys the symptomatic nidus while minimizing damage to surrounding bone?
explanation: Image-guided thermal ablation targets the osteoid osteoma nidus while sparing surrounding bone.
optionFeedback: Image-guided thermal ablation targets the osteoid osteoma nidus while sparing surrounding bone.
Chemotherapy is not indicated for a benign osteoid osteoma.
Wide resection is unnecessarily extensive for this typical small lesion.
Radiation is not the usual definitive treatment for osteoid osteoma.

distractors.B: Chemotherapy is not indicated for a benign osteoid osteoma.
distractors.C: Wide resection is unnecessarily extensive for this typical small lesion.
distractors.D: Radiation is not the usual definitive treatment for osteoid osteoma.

stem: A 36-year-old male undergoes evaluation for an incidentally discovered cartilaginous lesion within a metacarpal. Histology reveals benign chondrocytes surrounded by a cartilaginous matrix. Molecular testing demonstrates an abnormality involving isocitrate dehydrogenase. Which of the following cellular processes is most closely associated with the molecular pathogenesis of this lesion?
options: Activation of osteoclasts through RANK signaling
Loss of retinoblastoma protein-mediated cell-cycle regulation
explanation: Mutant IDH produces 2-hydroxyglutarate, which alters epigenetic regulation including DNA methylation.
optionFeedback: Beta-catenin stabilization is associated with desmoid tumors.
RANK signaling is relevant to giant cell tumor.
Mutant IDH produces 2-hydroxyglutarate, which alters epigenetic regulation including DNA methylation.
RB1 loss is associated with osteosarcoma predisposition.

distractors.A: Beta-catenin stabilization is associated with desmoid tumors.
distractors.B: RANK signaling is relevant to giant cell tumor.
distractors.D: RB1 loss is associated with osteosarcoma predisposition.

stem: A 55-year-old female undergoes surgical resection of a large conventional chondrosarcoma involving the pelvis. The final pathology report describes marked cellularity, severe nuclear pleomorphism, and numerous mitotic figures. Compared with a low-grade tumor of the same histologic lineage, which of the following outcomes is most likely?
options: Loss of the ability to infiltrate surrounding bone
explanation: Higher-grade chondrosarcoma has greater metastatic potential and worse prognosis.
optionFeedback: Higher grade does not confer a lower local recurrence risk.
Higher-grade chondrosarcoma has greater metastatic potential and worse prognosis.
Spontaneous regression is not characteristic of high-grade chondrosarcoma.
Infiltrative growth is a malignant feature and is not lost with higher grade.

distractors.A: Higher grade does not confer a lower local recurrence risk.
distractors.C: Spontaneous regression is not characteristic of high-grade chondrosarcoma.
distractors.D: Infiltrative growth is a malignant feature and is not lost with higher grade.

stem: A 13-year-old female with a family history of sarcomas, early-onset breast cancer, and brain tumors develops a destructive bone lesion in the distal femur. Histologic examination demonstrates malignant osteoid production. Her physician suspects an inherited cancer predisposition syndrome. Which of the following molecular abnormalities is most likely responsible?
explanation: Li-Fraumeni syndrome results from germline TP53 pathogenic variants and predisposes to osteosarcoma and other early cancers.
optionFeedback: GNAS activation causes fibrous dysplasia.
CDK4 amplification is associated with certain sarcomas but does not explain this inherited constellation.
EWSR1 rearrangement is characteristic of Ewing sarcoma.
Li-Fraumeni syndrome results from germline TP53 pathogenic variants and predisposes to osteosarcoma and other early cancers.

distractors.A: GNAS activation causes fibrous dysplasia.
distractors.B: CDK4 amplification is associated with certain sarcomas but does not explain this inherited constellation.
distractors.C: EWSR1 rearrangement is characteristic of Ewing sarcoma.

stem: A 12-year-old boy is evaluated for asymmetry of the chest wall. Imaging reveals an expansile rib lesion with a ground-glass appearance. There are no additional skeletal abnormalities, skin findings, or endocrine manifestations. Biopsy demonstrates benign fibroblastic tissue surrounding irregular trabeculae of immature bone. Which of the following mechanisms best explains the development of this lesion?
options: Abnormal osteoblastic differentiation due to an activating somatic mutation
Uncontrolled proliferation of growth plate chondrocytes due to an EXT mutation
Formation of a fusion transcription factor following t(11;22)
explanation: Monostotic fibrous dysplasia arises from mosaic activating GNAS mutations that disrupt normal osteogenic differentiation.
optionFeedback: Monostotic fibrous dysplasia arises from mosaic activating GNAS mutations that disrupt normal osteogenic differentiation.
The lesion is not a malignancy of osteoclasts.
EXT mutations cause hereditary multiple osteochondromas.
The t(11;22) fusion is associated with Ewing sarcoma.

distractors.B: The lesion is not a malignancy of osteoclasts.
distractors.C: EXT mutations cause hereditary multiple osteochondromas.
distractors.D: The t(11;22) fusion is associated with Ewing sarcoma.

stem: A 69-year-old female with a history of breast carcinoma develops persistent pain in the lumbar spine. Imaging reveals several destructive vertebral lesions. Biopsy demonstrates malignant epithelial cells arranged in glandular structures within the bone marrow. Which of the following classifications most accurately describes these skeletal lesions?
explanation: Malignant epithelial glands in bone with a history of breast cancer support metastatic carcinoma.
optionFeedback: Osteosarcoma produces malignant osteoid rather than epithelial glands.
Chondrosarcoma produces cartilaginous matrix.
Malignant epithelial glands in bone with a history of breast cancer support metastatic carcinoma.
Giant cell tumor has mononuclear stromal cells and reactive giant cells.

distractors.A: Osteosarcoma produces malignant osteoid rather than epithelial glands.
distractors.B: Chondrosarcoma produces cartilaginous matrix.
distractors.D: Giant cell tumor has mononuclear stromal cells and reactive giant cells.

stem: A 29-year-old male presents with a slowly enlarging bony mass involving the proximal tibia. The excised lesion consists of a central region of mature trabecular bone covered by orderly cartilage resembling a growth plate. Which of the following developmental processes most closely explains the formation of the bony component beneath its cartilage cap?
options: Intramembranous ossification without a cartilage precursor
Osteoclastic resorption without subsequent bone formation
Dystrophic calcification of necrotic skeletal muscle
explanation: Osteochondroma grows through endochondral ossification beneath its cartilage cap.
optionFeedback: Intramembranous ossification bypasses a cartilage template.
Osteochondroma grows through endochondral ossification beneath its cartilage cap.
Resorption alone cannot explain formation of mature trabecular bone.
Dystrophic calcification does not produce an organized growth plate-like cap.

distractors.A: Intramembranous ossification bypasses a cartilage template.
distractors.C: Resorption alone cannot explain formation of mature trabecular bone.
distractors.D: Dystrophic calcification does not produce an organized growth plate-like cap.

stem: A 14-year-old female is diagnosed with a malignant diaphyseal bone tumor characterized by an EWSR1-FLI1 fusion. Imaging demonstrates extensive cortical destruction and a large associated soft tissue mass. Which of the following treatment strategies is most consistent with management of this neoplasm?
options: NSAID therapy followed by radiofrequency ablation
Systemic chemotherapy combined with surgery and/or radiation therapy
explanation: Ewing sarcoma requires multimodal treatment with systemic chemotherapy and local control by surgery and/or radiation.
optionFeedback: Ewing sarcoma requires active oncologic treatment.
NSAIDs and ablation are appropriate for selected osteoid osteomas, not Ewing sarcoma.
Local curettage alone does not address systemic disease risk.
Ewing sarcoma requires multimodal treatment with systemic chemotherapy and local control by surgery and/or radiation.

distractors.A: Ewing sarcoma requires active oncologic treatment.
distractors.B: NSAIDs and ablation are appropriate for selected osteoid osteomas, not Ewing sarcoma.
distractors.C: Local curettage alone does not address systemic disease risk.

stem: A 34-year-old female previously underwent curettage and cementing of an expansile epiphyseal tumor involving the distal femur. Follow-up imaging demonstrates a recurrent lesion at the operative site. The original tumor contained numerous reactive osteoclast-like giant cells but lacked malignant osteoid. Which of the following classifications best describes its typical biological behavior?
options: Intermediate, locally aggressive neoplasm with substantial recurrence risk but rare metastasis
Uniformly benign neoplasm with no capacity for local destruction
High-grade osteogenic malignancy with frequent pulmonary metastases
Malignant cartilage-forming neoplasm with grade-dependent metastatic potential
explanation: Giant cell tumor is locally aggressive, can recur after curettage and rarely metastasizes, often to lung.
optionFeedback: Giant cell tumor is locally aggressive, can recur after curettage and rarely metastasizes, often to lung.
Giant cell tumor can cause substantial local destruction.
Malignant osteoid is required for osteosarcoma.
Cartilage production would suggest a chondrogenic tumor.

distractors.B: Giant cell tumor can cause substantial local destruction.
distractors.C: Malignant osteoid is required for osteosarcoma.
distractors.D: Cartilage production would suggest a chondrogenic tumor.

stem: A 62-year-old male presents with progressive abdominal distension. Imaging demonstrates a 19-cm retroperitoneal mass containing adipose tissue and thickened internal septa. Histologic examination reveals atypical stromal cells, and molecular testing demonstrates amplification involving chromosome 12q. Which of the following additional genes may be coamplified with MDM2 in this lesion?
explanation: CDK4 and MDM2 are frequently coamplified in well-differentiated or dedifferentiated liposarcoma.
optionFeedback: GNAS is associated with fibrous dysplasia.
PAX3 participates in an alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma fusion.
CDK4 and MDM2 are frequently coamplified in well-differentiated or dedifferentiated liposarcoma.
EXT2 is associated with hereditary multiple exostoses.

distractors.A: GNAS is associated with fibrous dysplasia.
distractors.B: PAX3 participates in an alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma fusion.
distractors.D: EXT2 is associated with hereditary multiple exostoses.

stem: A 37-year-old female undergoes resection of a deep thigh mass. The specimen contains abundant gelatinous material, and microscopic examination reveals lipoblasts distributed among thin, branching vascular channels. Molecular studies identify a rearrangement involving chromosome 16. Which of the following chromosomal translocations is most consistent with these findings?
explanation: Myxoid liposarcoma classically has t(12;16), forming FUS-DDIT3.
optionFeedback: Myxoid liposarcoma classically has t(12;16), forming FUS-DDIT3.
t(11;22) forms EWSR1-FLI1 in Ewing sarcoma.
t(X;18) forms SS18-SSX in synovial sarcoma.
t(2;13) forms PAX3-FOXO1 in alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma.

distractors.B: t(11;22) forms EWSR1-FLI1 in Ewing sarcoma.
distractors.C: t(X;18) forms SS18-SSX in synovial sarcoma.
distractors.D: t(2;13) forms PAX3-FOXO1 in alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma.

stem: A 56-year-old male and a 60-year-old female are diagnosed with histologically similar well-differentiated adipocytic neoplasms. The male's tumor is located within the deep soft tissues of the thigh, whereas the female's tumor occupies the retroperitoneum and surrounds several abdominal structures. Which of the following factors most directly contributes to the greater management difficulty associated with the retroperitoneal lesion?
options: Difficulty obtaining complete surgical margins without damaging adjacent structures
explanation: Retroperitoneal anatomy makes complete resection challenging and increases the risk of local recurrence.
optionFeedback: Both lesions retain adipocytic differentiation.
Well-differentiated liposarcoma does not obligatorily spread via lymphatics.
MDM2 amplification may occur in both sites.
Retroperitoneal anatomy makes complete resection challenging and increases the risk of local recurrence.

distractors.A: Both lesions retain adipocytic differentiation.
distractors.B: Well-differentiated liposarcoma does not obligatorily spread via lymphatics.
distractors.C: MDM2 amplification may occur in both sites.

stem: A 32-year-old male with familial adenomatous polyposis develops an infiltrative mesenteric mass following abdominal surgery. Histologic examination reveals bland spindle-shaped fibroblasts arranged in long fascicles. Which of the following molecular mechanisms best connects his inherited condition with the development of this lesion?
options: Constitutive activation of RANK ligand signaling
Impaired degradation and accumulation of beta-catenin
Overexpression of an EWSR1-FLI1 fusion protein
Amplification of genes regulating adipocytic differentiation
explanation: APC loss impairs beta-catenin degradation, activating Wnt signaling in FAP-associated desmoid tumors.
optionFeedback: RANKL signaling recruits osteoclasts in giant cell tumor.
APC loss impairs beta-catenin degradation, activating Wnt signaling in FAP-associated desmoid tumors.
EWSR1-FLI1 drives Ewing sarcoma.
MDM2/CDK4 amplification is associated with adipocytic sarcomas.

distractors.A: RANKL signaling recruits osteoclasts in giant cell tumor.
distractors.C: EWSR1-FLI1 drives Ewing sarcoma.
distractors.D: MDM2/CDK4 amplification is associated with adipocytic sarcomas.

stem: A 61-year-old male reports progressive curvature of his penis during erection. Physical examination identifies a firm fibrous plaque along its dorsal surface. He has no systemic symptoms or evidence of distant disease. Which of the following conditions represents a manifestation of a similar underlying fibroproliferative process at a different anatomical site?
explanation: Peyronie disease and Dupuytren contracture are related benign fibroproliferative disorders.
optionFeedback: Rhabdomyosarcoma is a malignant skeletal muscle-lineage tumor.
Liposarcoma is an adipocytic malignancy.
Peyronie disease and Dupuytren contracture are related benign fibroproliferative disorders.
Synovial sarcoma is a distinct fusion-driven malignancy.

distractors.A: Rhabdomyosarcoma is a malignant skeletal muscle-lineage tumor.
distractors.B: Liposarcoma is an adipocytic malignancy.
distractors.D: Synovial sarcoma is a distinct fusion-driven malignancy.

stem: A 45-year-old female undergoes surgical removal of a small, mobile subcutaneous mass from her upper arm. Histopathology demonstrates mature adipocytes without atypical stromal cells, necrosis, or mitotic abnormalities. Which of the following outcomes is most likely following complete simple excision?
options: Cure with a low likelihood of recurrence
Predictable progression to a high-grade liposarcoma
Early spread to regional lymph nodes
explanation: Ordinary lipoma is benign and complete excision is usually curative.
optionFeedback: Ordinary lipoma is benign and complete excision is usually curative.
Typical lipomas do not predictably transform into liposarcoma.
Lipomas do not metastasize.
Adjuvant chemotherapy is not needed for ordinary lipoma.

distractors.B: Typical lipomas do not predictably transform into liposarcoma.
distractors.C: Lipomas do not metastasize.
distractors.D: Adjuvant chemotherapy is not needed for ordinary lipoma.

stem: A 57-year-old female with a history of uterine fibroids develops a newly diagnosed malignant uterine smooth muscle tumor. During counseling, she asks whether the malignancy necessarily arose from one of her longstanding benign fibroids. Which of the following statements most accurately describes the usual pathogenesis of this malignant neoplasm?
options: It develops exclusively from longstanding uterine leiomyomas.
It develops through malignant transformation of endometrial glands.
It develops from immature skeletal muscle precursors.
It usually arises de novo rather than through transformation of a typical leiomyoma.
explanation: Leiomyosarcoma generally arises de novo as a malignant smooth muscle neoplasm.
optionFeedback: Most uterine leiomyosarcomas do not arise from ordinary fibroids.
Endometrial glands are epithelial rather than smooth muscle.
Skeletal muscle differentiation describes rhabdomyosarcoma.
Leiomyosarcoma generally arises de novo as a malignant smooth muscle neoplasm.

distractors.A: Most uterine leiomyosarcomas do not arise from ordinary fibroids.
distractors.B: Endometrial glands are epithelial rather than smooth muscle.
distractors.C: Skeletal muscle differentiation describes rhabdomyosarcoma.

stem: A 48-year-old female undergoes surgical resection of a well-circumscribed uterine mass for persistent pelvic discomfort. Microscopy reveals intersecting fascicles of uniform spindle cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm. Which of the following additional findings would raise the greatest concern for malignant rather than benign smooth muscle differentiation?
options: Marked atypia, frequent mitoses, and tumor cell necrosis
explanation: Marked atypia, elevated mitotic activity and tumor cell necrosis support leiomyosarcoma.
optionFeedback: Blunt-ended nuclei are typical of smooth muscle in benign and malignant lesions.
Marked atypia, elevated mitotic activity and tumor cell necrosis support leiomyosarcoma.
Whorled fascicles occur in leiomyoma.
Uniform eosinophilic cytoplasm indicates differentiation rather than malignancy.

distractors.A: Blunt-ended nuclei are typical of smooth muscle in benign and malignant lesions.
distractors.C: Whorled fascicles occur in leiomyoma.
distractors.D: Uniform eosinophilic cytoplasm indicates differentiation rather than malignancy.

stem: A 5-year-old boy presents with urinary obstruction and intermittent hematuria. Imaging reveals a soft tissue mass projecting into the bladder lumen. Biopsy demonstrates malignant cells with elongated eosinophilic cytoplasm and features of skeletal muscle differentiation. Which of the following tumor subtypes is most consistent with the patient's age and anatomical location?
explanation: Embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma occurs in children and can involve the genitourinary tract, including the bladder.
optionFeedback: Liposarcoma exhibits adipocytic differentiation.
Synovial sarcoma more commonly occurs in deep extremity soft tissue of young adults.
Embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma occurs in children and can involve the genitourinary tract, including the bladder.
Leiomyosarcoma exhibits smooth rather than skeletal muscle differentiation.

distractors.A: Liposarcoma exhibits adipocytic differentiation.
distractors.B: Synovial sarcoma more commonly occurs in deep extremity soft tissue of young adults.
distractors.D: Leiomyosarcoma exhibits smooth rather than skeletal muscle differentiation.

stem: A 17-year-old male presents with a deep soft tissue mass in the thigh and enlarged regional lymph nodes. Histopathologic examination identifies an alveolar growth pattern, and molecular studies demonstrate a PAX3-FOXO1 fusion. Compared with the more common embryonal subtype, which of the following characteristics is most consistent with this tumor?
options: Less favorable prognosis and greater concern for metastatic disease
Predominant occurrence in the infant myocardium
Absence of malignant skeletal muscle differentiation
explanation: Fusion-positive alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma generally has a worse prognosis and greater metastatic risk.
optionFeedback: Fusion-positive alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma generally has a worse prognosis and greater metastatic risk.
This is a malignant sarcoma.
Cardiac rhabdomyoma is the benign infant myocardial tumor.
Alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma exhibits malignant skeletal muscle differentiation.

distractors.B: This is a malignant sarcoma.
distractors.C: Cardiac rhabdomyoma is the benign infant myocardial tumor.
distractors.D: Alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma exhibits malignant skeletal muscle differentiation.

stem: A 58-year-old male presents with a painless mass within the oral cavity that has slowly enlarged over several years. Histopathologic examination demonstrates benign skeletal muscle differentiation without significant atypia or infiltrative growth. Which of the following neoplasms is most consistent with these findings?
explanation: Adult extracardiac rhabdomyoma is a benign skeletal muscle tumor often found in the head and neck.
optionFeedback: Leiomyoma displays smooth muscle differentiation.
Deep fibromatosis is a fibroblastic lesion with infiltrative growth.
Alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma is malignant.
Adult extracardiac rhabdomyoma is a benign skeletal muscle tumor often found in the head and neck.

distractors.A: Leiomyoma displays smooth muscle differentiation.
distractors.B: Deep fibromatosis is a fibroblastic lesion with infiltrative growth.
distractors.C: Alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma is malignant.

stem: A 26-year-old female undergoes biopsy of a deep soft tissue mass adjacent to the ankle. Histologic examination reveals predominantly spindle-shaped cells without clearly identifiable glandular structures. Molecular analysis demonstrates an SS18-SSX fusion. Which of the following interpretations best accounts for these findings?
options: Synovial sarcoma is excluded because the lesion lacks epithelial glands.
The lesion is consistent with monophasic synovial sarcoma.
The fusion establishes a diagnosis of myxoid liposarcoma.
The lesion must arise directly from the synovial membrane.
explanation: SS18-SSX supports synovial sarcoma, including the monophasic spindle-cell form.
optionFeedback: Monophasic synovial sarcoma may lack glandular structures.
SS18-SSX supports synovial sarcoma, including the monophasic spindle-cell form.
Myxoid liposarcoma typically carries FUS-DDIT3.
Synovial sarcoma need not originate from synovium.

distractors.A: Monophasic synovial sarcoma may lack glandular structures.
distractors.C: Myxoid liposarcoma typically carries FUS-DDIT3.
distractors.D: Synovial sarcoma need not originate from synovium.

stem: A 72-year-old male presents with a large, rapidly enlarging deep soft tissue mass of the thigh. Histopathologic examination demonstrates malignant pleomorphic cells with extensive necrosis. After comprehensive histologic and ancillary evaluation, the pathologist cannot identify specific adipocytic, muscular, or other recognizable lineage differentiation. Which of the following diagnostic categories is most appropriate?
explanation: Undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma is a diagnosis of exclusion after investigation fails to identify a specific lineage.
optionFeedback: Superficial fibromatosis is a benign fibroproliferative process.
Well-differentiated liposarcoma shows adipocytic lineage.
Undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma is a diagnosis of exclusion after investigation fails to identify a specific lineage.
Leiomyoma is a benign smooth muscle tumor.

distractors.A: Superficial fibromatosis is a benign fibroproliferative process.
distractors.B: Well-differentiated liposarcoma shows adipocytic lineage.
distractors.D: Leiomyoma is a benign smooth muscle tumor.

stem: A 64-year-old female undergoes wide local excision of a high-grade soft tissue sarcoma involving the proximal lower extremity. The final pathology report describes viable malignant cells extending to the inked surgical margin. Which of the following outcomes is most directly predicted by this particular finding?
options: Increased risk of local tumor recurrence
Development of an inherited tumor predisposition syndrome
Conversion to a benign histologic phenotype
Reduced likelihood of residual local disease
explanation: An involved margin suggests residual microscopic tumor and increases local recurrence risk.
optionFeedback: An involved margin suggests residual microscopic tumor and increases local recurrence risk.
Margin status does not cause inherited predisposition.
Positive margins do not change malignant lineage into benign tissue.
Tumor at the inked margin increases rather than reduces concern for residual disease.

distractors.B: Margin status does not cause inherited predisposition.
distractors.C: Positive margins do not change malignant lineage into benign tissue.
distractors.D: Tumor at the inked margin increases rather than reduces concern for residual disease.

stem: A 49-year-old male is diagnosed with a 12-cm high-grade intramuscular sarcoma. Before definitive management, the oncology team performs staging studies. The patient asks why imaging of his chest is necessary when his tumor is confined clinically to the thigh. Which of the following explanations is most appropriate?
options: Soft tissue sarcomas spread exclusively through regional lymph nodes.
Most soft tissue sarcomas originate from pulmonary epithelial cells.
Chest imaging is required only when a patient reports respiratory symptoms.
Hematogenous spread to the lungs is a common metastatic pattern of soft tissue sarcomas.
explanation: Lungs are a common site of hematogenous metastasis, making chest staging important.
optionFeedback: Most soft tissue sarcomas spread primarily hematogenously, although some subtypes spread to nodes.
Sarcomas are mesenchymal rather than pulmonary epithelial tumors.
Pulmonary metastases may be asymptomatic, so staging is not symptom-dependent.
Lungs are a common site of hematogenous metastasis, making chest staging important.

distractors.A: Most soft tissue sarcomas spread primarily hematogenously, although some subtypes spread to nodes.
distractors.B: Sarcomas are mesenchymal rather than pulmonary epithelial tumors.
distractors.C: Pulmonary metastases may be asymptomatic, so staging is not symptom-dependent.
